definition: Reformulations of attention with kernel tricks so cost grows linearly with sequence length, trading some quality for the ability to handle very long sequences and constant-memory inference.
details: Reformulations of attention with kernel tricks so cost grows linearly with sequence length, trading some quality for the ability to handle very long sequences and constant-memory inference.

explainer.lead: Linear attention reformulates attention using kernel tricks so that cost grows linearly with sequence length. It matters for handling very long sequences and enabling constant-memory inference, trading some quality for efficiency.

tiers.eli5: Instead of comparing every word with every other word (which gets slow for long texts), it uses a shortcut that scales better, like summarizing the conversation as you go.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use linear attention to reduce memory and compute for long-context models; a pitfall is that the approximation can degrade quality on tasks requiring precise long-range dependencies compared to standard attention.
tiers.paperLevel: Linear attention uses kernel tricks to reformulate attention so cost is O(n) in sequence length, enabling constant-memory inference; its known limit is a quality trade-off versus quadratic attention.

explainer.example: A language model processing a 10,000-token document uses linear attention to keep inference memory constant, whereas standard attention would require memory growing with the square of the length.
